A.reason: All candidates preserve destination privacy, permit emergency use when the bike is present, and compare the three required measures over two weeks. Mechanisms are first-entry reservations, rotating priority, recent-use fairness, flexible scheduling, bounded checkout queues, and voluntary return between riding legs. Candidate 5 best combines low administration, early conflict detection and explicit late-return recovery. Its idle-time measure should include booked-but-unused time as well as unclaimed time.

B.reason: All candidates satisfy the hard constraints. Their distinct mechanisms are first-entry reservations, rotating priority, recent-use fairness, flexible scheduling, and bounded checkout queues. Candidate 0 is the strongest default: simple, practical for irregular trips, private, and directly inspectable through missed trips, unused time and coordination effort. The alternatives depend more on predictable demand, acceptable fairness rules or flexible departure times.

pair.reason: A5 narrowly improves on B0 by addressing late returns, a concrete source of last-minute conflicts, without requiring daily scheduling or usage-history bookkeeping. B0 has the cleaner overall idle-time measure, but A5's recovery rule offers a practical reliability benefit with little routine overhead. Neither proposal establishes results before the trial.
